newsitem.title: USA: Forbes calls budget deal Clinton spending spree.
newsitem.headline: Forbes calls budget deal Clinton spending spree.

text.p: Conservative Republican Steve Forbes Wednesday attacked a bipartisan balanced budget agreement as a "big government spending spree."
Forbes, who ran for the Republican presidential nomination last year and is thinking of running again in 2000, launched a television and radio campaign attacking the budget deal.

"Congress has a moral obligation to either fix or reject a deal that's clearly a big government spending spree with pitifully poor tax cuts," Forbes said in a statement issued by his advocacy organization, Americans for Hope, Growth and Opportunity."

He said the deal, reached May 2 between Clinton and Republican leaders of Congress, provided only $17 billion in net tax cuts per year -- which he said was less than one percent of annual federal spending of more than $1.7 trillion.
The plan includes a net $85 billion in tax cuts. The White House and Republicans are currently in a tussle over the direction of the tax cuts.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry, asked to respond, said the ad campaign seems directed at Forbes' fellow Republicans in addition to Clinton.
"So it's more an example of this internecine warfare under way in the Republican Party, which is quite entertaining to watch," McCurry said.
A Forbes spokesman said the TV ad was being aired in Washington and the radio ad in 11 different markets.
